original.text: 設我得佛，國中人天不住定聚必至滅度者，不取正覺。
original.edition: Taishō T12n0360 (CBETA XML P5, local copy sources_raw/cbeta), 268a11-12
original.licence: CBETA CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 (text quoted for reference)

paraphrase: The eleventh vow: if, when he attains buddhahood, the humans and gods of his land do not dwell in the rightly established group and necessarily reach extinction (nirvāṇa), may he not attain perfect awakening.
speaker: Dharmākara
notes: Shinran's 'vow of necessary attainment of nirvāṇa' (Realization chapter).

original.text: 設我得佛，光明有能限量，下至不照百千億那由他諸佛國者，不取正覺。設我得佛，壽命有能限量，下至百千億那由他劫者，不取正覺。
original.edition: Taishō T12n0360 (CBETA XML P5, local copy sources_raw/cbeta), 268a13-16
original.licence: CBETA CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 (text quoted for reference)

paraphrase: The twelfth and thirteenth vows: his light shall not be limited so as not to illuminate hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of buddha-lands, and his life shall not be limited to hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of kalpas — else may he not attain awakening.
speaker: Dharmākara
notes: Shinran reads these as the vows establishing the true Buddha and land.

original.text: 設我得佛，十方世界無量諸佛不悉咨嗟稱我名者，不取正覺。
original.edition: Taishō T12n0360 (CBETA XML P5, local copy sources_raw/cbeta), 268a24-25
original.licence: CBETA CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 (text quoted for reference)

paraphrase: The seventeenth vow: if the immeasurable buddhas of the worlds in the ten directions do not all praise and call his name, may he not attain awakening.
speaker: Dharmākara
notes: Shinran's 'vow that all buddhas say the name', the source of the great practice (Gyō chapter).

original.text: 設我得佛，十方眾生發菩提心修諸功德，至心發願欲生我國，臨壽終時，假令不與大眾圍遶現其人前者，不取正覺。
original.edition: Taishō T12n0360 (CBETA XML P5, local copy sources_raw/cbeta), 268a29-b02
original.licence: CBETA CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 (text quoted for reference)

paraphrase: The nineteenth vow: beings of the ten directions who arouse the aspiration for awakening, cultivate meritorious practices and sincerely aspire to be born in his land — if at the end of their lives he does not appear before them surrounded by the great assembly, may he not attain awakening.
speaker: Dharmākara
notes: Shinran's 'vow of the practice of various goods', leading to the transformed land.

original.text: 設我得佛，十方眾生聞我名號、係念我國，殖諸德本、至心迴向欲生我國，不果遂者，不取正覺。
original.edition: Taishō T12n0360 (CBETA XML P5, local copy sources_raw/cbeta), 268b03-05
original.licence: CBETA CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 (text quoted for reference)

paraphrase: The twentieth vow: beings who hear his name, fix their thoughts on his land, plant the roots of virtue and sincerely dedicate them wishing to be born there — if they do not in the end succeed, may he not attain awakening.
speaker: Dharmākara
notes: Shinran's 'vow of accumulating merit', the self-power nenbutsu.

original.text: 設我得佛，他方佛土諸菩薩眾來生我國，究竟必至一生補處——除其本願自在所化，為眾生故，被弘誓鎧，積累德本度脫一切
original.edition: Taishō T12n0360 (CBETA XML P5, local copy sources_raw/cbeta), 268b08-10
original.licence: CBETA CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 (text quoted for reference)

paraphrase: The twenty-second vow: bodhisattvas from other lands born in his land will certainly reach the stage of one life from buddhahood — except those who by their own vow freely choose to teach, donning the armour of great vows for beings' sake, accumulating merit to save all, travelling to buddha-lands and practising the virtue of Samantabhadra.
speaker: Dharmākara
notes: Tanluan and Shinran read it as the vow of returning (gensō).

original.text: 設我得佛，十方無量不可思議諸佛世界，其有女人聞我名字，歡喜信樂，發菩提心，厭惡女身，壽終之後復為女像者，不取正覺。
original.edition: Taishō T12n0360 (CBETA XML P5, local copy sources_raw/cbeta), 268c21-24
original.licence: CBETA CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 (text quoted for reference)

paraphrase: The thirty-fifth vow: if women in the immeasurable worlds of the ten directions who hear his name, rejoice with faith, arouse the aspiration for awakening and are weary of a female body should again take female form after death, may he not attain awakening.
speaker: Dharmākara
notes: Recorded faithfully; cf. the Rebirth Treatise's 'no women ... are born there' and the Jingtu shiyi lun's reading (T1961 80b05).

original.text: 必得超絕去，往生安養國。橫截五惡趣，惡趣自然閉；昇道無窮極，易往而無人。
original.edition: Taishō T12n0360 (CBETA XML P5, local copy sources_raw/cbeta), 274b22-24
original.licence: CBETA CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 (text quoted for reference)

paraphrase: Strive and you will surely transcend and go to be born in the land of Peace and Sustenance, cutting crosswise through the five evil destinies, which close of themselves; the ascent on the way is without limit; it is easy to go there, yet there is no one who goes.
speaker: Śākyamuni
notes: 'Cutting crosswise' (橫截) is the basis of Shinran's 'crosswise transcendence'.

original.text: 今我於此世間作佛，處於五惡、五痛、五燒之中，為最劇苦。教化群生令捨五惡、令去五痛、令離五燒
original.edition: Taishō T12n0360 (CBETA XML P5, local copy sources_raw/cbeta), 275c20-22
original.licence: CBETA CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 (text quoted for reference)

paraphrase: The Buddha tells Maitreya that the buddha-lands elsewhere are easy to transform because their beings do good of themselves, whereas he has become a buddha in this world amid the five evils, five pains and five burnings, the most severe suffering; he teaches beings to abandon them and keep the five goods.
speaker: Śākyamuni

original.text: 憍慢弊懈怠，難以信此法；宿世見諸佛，樂聽如是教。
original.edition: Taishō T12n0360 (CBETA XML P5, local copy sources_raw/cbeta), 273b03-04
original.licence: CBETA CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 (text quoted for reference)

paraphrase: Those who are arrogant, corrupt and lazy find it hard to believe this teaching; those who have seen buddhas in past lives delight to hear it; the ocean of the Tathāgata's wisdom is beyond the measure of śrāvakas and bodhisattvas; only a buddha fully knows it.
speaker: Śākyamuni

original.text: 若有眾生以疑惑心修諸功德，願生彼國，不了佛智、不思議智、不可稱智、大乘廣智、無等無倫最上勝智，於此諸智疑惑不信；然猶信罪福，修習善本，願生其國。此諸眾生生彼宮殿，壽五百歲，常不見佛、不聞經法、不見菩薩聲聞聖眾，是故於彼國土謂之胎生。
original.edition: Taishō T12n0360 (CBETA XML P5, local copy sources_raw/cbeta), 278a22-28
original.licence: CBETA CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 (text quoted for reference)

paraphrase: Those who cultivate merit and aspire to birth while doubting the Buddha's inconceivable and unequalled wisdom — yet believing in sin and merit and cultivating good roots — are born in palaces there where for five hundred years they do not see the Buddha, hear the teaching or see the holy assembly; this is called womb-birth; those who clearly believe in the Buddha's wisdom are born by transformation, seated in lotuses.
speaker: Śākyamuni

original.text: 其有得聞彼佛名號，歡喜踊躍，乃至一念，當知此人為得大利，則是具足無上功德。
original.edition: Taishō T12n0360 (CBETA XML P5, local copy sources_raw/cbeta), 279a01-03
original.licence: CBETA CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 (text quoted for reference)

paraphrase: The Buddha tells Maitreya: whoever hears that Buddha's name and rejoices, even for a single thought, should be known to have gained the great benefit — to be endowed with unsurpassed merit.
speaker: Śākyamuni
notes: Cited by Hōnen (Senchakushū ch. 5) and Shinran for the 'one thought'.

original.text: 當來之世經道滅盡，我以慈悲哀愍特留此經止住百歲，其有眾生值斯經者，隨意所願皆可得度。
original.edition: Taishō T12n0360 (CBETA XML P5, local copy sources_raw/cbeta), 279a11-13
original.licence: CBETA CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 (text quoted for reference)

paraphrase: In the age to come when the scriptures and the way have perished, out of compassion the Buddha will keep this sūtra alone for a hundred years more; beings who meet it will all be saved according to their wish.
speaker: Śākyamuni
notes: Hōnen's Senchakushū ch. 6 (the nenbutsu alone remains).

original.text: 若聞斯經信樂受持，難中之難無過此難。
original.edition: Taishō T12n0360 (CBETA XML P5, local copy sources_raw/cbeta), 279a16-17
original.licence: CBETA CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 (text quoted for reference)

paraphrase: It is hard to meet a Tathāgata, hard to hear the scriptures, hard to hear the perfections, hard to meet a good teacher and practise; but to hear this sūtra and joyfully entrust oneself and hold to it — of all difficulties none surpasses this.
speaker: Śākyamuni
notes: Echoed in the Shōshinge ('difficult among difficulties').

original.text: sacen me bhagavan bodhiprāptasyāprameyāsaṃkhyeyeṣu buddhakṣetreṣu ye sattvāḥ mama nāmadheyaṃ śrutvā, tatra buddhakṣetre cittaṃ preṣayeyur, upapattaye kuśalamūlāni ca pariṇāmayeyus, te ca tatra buddhakṣetre nopapadyeran, antaśo daśabhiś cittotpādaparivartaiḥ, sthāpayitvānantaryakāriṇaḥ saddharmapratikṣepāvaraṇāvṛtāṃś ca sattvān, mā tāvad aham anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim abhisaṃbudhyeyam
original.edition: Sukhāvatīvyūha, data entry Y. Fujita (GRETIL; local sources_raw/dcs/corpus/GRETIL/sa_sukhAvatIvyUha.txt, line 94)
original.licence: GRETIL e-text quoted for reference

paraphrase: Sanskrit vow 19: if beings in immeasurable buddha-fields who hear his name direct their minds to his field and dedicate their roots of good for birth there should not be born there — even by as few as ten turnings of the arising of thought — excepting those who have committed the deeds of immediate retribution and those obstructed by rejecting the true Dharma, may he not awaken.
speaker: Dharmākara

differs_from.note: The Sanskrit counts this as vow 19 of 47 and speaks of 'ten turnings of the arising of thought' and dedication of roots of good, where T360 (vow 18 of 48) has 'sincerely entrusting and joyful, ... even ten nian'.

notes: Correction to common statements: the Sanskrit text in GRETIL numbers 47 vows; the Chinese T360 has 48.

original.text: ye sattvā anyeṣu lokadhātuṣv anuttarāyāḥ samyaksaṃbodheś cittam utpādya, mama nāmadheyaṃ śrutvā, prasannacittā mām anusmareyus, teṣāṃ ced ahaṃ maraṇakālasamaye pratyupasthite bhikṣusaṃghaparivṛtaḥ puraskṛto na puratas tiṣṭheyam, yad idaṃ : cittāvikṣepatāyai
original.edition: Sukhāvatīvyūha, data entry Y. Fujita (GRETIL; local copy, line 93)
original.licence: GRETIL e-text quoted for reference

paraphrase: Sanskrit vow 18: beings in other worlds who have aroused the thought of awakening, heard his name and recollect him with a serene mind — at the time of their death he will stand before them surrounded by the assembly of monks, so that their minds are not distracted.
speaker: Dharmākara
notes: Corresponds to T360's nineteenth vow.

original.text: ye te 'jita bodhisattvā anyeṣu buddhakṣetreṣu sthitāḥ sukhāvatyāṃ lokadhātāv upapattaye vicikitsām utpādayanti, tena cittena kuśalamūlāny avaropayanti, teṣām atra garbhāvāso bhavati
original.edition: Sukhāvatīvyūha, Fujita (GRETIL; local copy, line 375)
original.licence: GRETIL e-text quoted for reference

paraphrase: The Buddha tells Ajita (Maitreya): those who plant roots of good for birth in Sukhāvatī with doubt dwell there within the lotus as in a womb; those free of doubt, who trust the unobstructed knowledge of the buddhas, appear seated cross-legged in lotuses by apparitional birth.
speaker: Śākyamuni

original.text: नावरमात्रकेण शारिपुत्र कुशलमूलेन अमितायुषस्तथागतस्य बुद्धक्षेत्रे सत्त्वा उपपद्यन्ते । यः कश्चिच्छारिपुत्र कुलपुत्रो वा कुलदुहिता वा तस्य भगवतो ऽमितायुषस्तथागतस्य नामधेयं श्रोष्यति, श्रुत्वा च मनसिकरिष्यति, एकरात्रं वा द्विरात्रं वा त्रिरात्रं वा चतूरात्रं वा पञ्चरात्रं वा षड्रात्रं वा सप्तरात्रं वाविक्षिप्तचित्तो मनसिकरिष्यति
original.edition: Sukhāvatīvyūha (saṃkṣiptamātṛkā), ed. P. L. Vaidya 1961, GRETIL Devanāgarī e-text (local copy), §10
original.licence: GRETIL e-text quoted for reference

paraphrase: Beings are not born in Amitāyus's field by a small root of good. Whoever hears the name of Amitāyus and keeps it in mind, keeping it in mind with undistracted thought for one night up to seven nights, will at death see Amitāyus standing before him with his assembly, will die with an unconfused mind and be born in Sukhāvatī; therefore one should earnestly aspire to that field.
speaker: Śākyamuni

differs_from.note: Sanskrit has 'hearing the name ... bringing to mind (manasikariṣyati)' for one to seven nights; Kumārajīva has 'holding fast to the name' (執持名號) for one to seven days — the Chinese wording underlies the East Asian reading as oral recitation.

original.text: 唯願世尊，為我廣說無憂惱處，我當往生，不樂閻浮提濁惡世也。
original.edition: Taishō T12n0365 (CBETA XML P5, local copy sources_raw/cbeta), 341b16-17
original.licence: CBETA CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 (text quoted for reference)

paraphrase: Vaidehī, imprisoned by her son, throws herself down weeping before the Buddha: what past sin made her bear such a son? She begs him to teach her of a place without sorrow where she may be born, for she no longer delights in this defiled and evil Jambudvīpa full of hells, hungry ghosts and animals.
speaker: Vaidehī

original.text: 我今樂生極樂世界阿彌陀佛所。唯願世尊，教我思惟，教我正受。
original.edition: Taishō T12n0365 (CBETA XML P5, local copy sources_raw/cbeta), 341b28-c01
original.licence: CBETA CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 (text quoted for reference)

paraphrase: Shown all the pure lands of the ten directions in the Buddha's light, Vaidehī chooses to be born in the Land of Bliss of Amitābha and asks to be taught how to think on it and how to receive it rightly.
speaker: Vaidehī
notes: Shandao reads 'thinking' and 'right reception' as the preparatory and full contemplation; the Chinese Pure Land tradition calls her request the 'selection' of the West.

original.text: 欲生彼國者，當修三福：一者、孝養父母，奉事師長，慈心不殺，修十善業。二者、受持三歸，具足眾戒，不犯威儀。三者、發菩提心，深信因果，讀誦大乘，勸進行者。如此三事名為淨業。
original.edition: Taishō T12n0365 (CBETA XML P5, local copy sources_raw/cbeta), 341c08-13
original.licence: CBETA CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 (text quoted for reference)

paraphrase: Amitābha is not far from here. Those who wish to be born there should cultivate three meritorious acts: caring for parents, serving teachers, not killing out of compassion, practising the ten good deeds; taking the three refuges, keeping the precepts, not breaching deportment; arousing the aspiration for awakening, deeply believing in cause and effect, reciting the Mahāyāna sūtras and encouraging others. These are the pure acts that are the right cause of the buddhas of the three times.
speaker: Śākyamuni

original.text: 汝是凡夫，心想羸劣，未得天眼，不能遠觀；諸佛如來有異方便，令汝得見。
original.edition: Taishō T12n0365 (CBETA XML P5, local copy sources_raw/cbeta), 341c23-24
original.licence: CBETA CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 (text quoted for reference)

paraphrase: The Buddha tells Vaidehī: you are an ordinary being, your mind and thought are weak, you lack the divine eye and cannot see far; the Tathāgatas have special means to let you see. She asks how beings after the Buddha's passing, defiled and pressed by the five sufferings, will see Amitābha's land.
speaker: Śākyamuni
notes: Key text for Shandao's thesis that the sūtra was taught for ordinary beings.

original.text: 無量壽佛有八萬四千相；一一相中，各有八萬四千隨形好；一一好中復有八萬四千光明；一一光明遍照十方世界，念佛眾生攝取不捨。
original.edition: Taishō T12n0365 (CBETA XML P5, local copy sources_raw/cbeta), 343b23-26
original.licence: CBETA CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 (text quoted for reference)

paraphrase: Ninth contemplation, of Amitāyus's true body: he has eighty-four thousand marks, each with eighty-four thousand minor marks, each with eighty-four thousand rays of light; each ray shines throughout the worlds of the ten directions and embraces, never abandoning, the beings who recollect the Buddha. One who sees this sees all buddhas; this is the samādhi of recollecting the Buddha; seeing the Buddha's body one sees the Buddha's mind, which is great compassion.
speaker: Śākyamuni

original.text: 若念佛者，當知此人即是人中芬陀利花，觀世音菩薩、大勢至菩薩為其勝友，當坐道場，生諸佛家。」佛告阿難：「汝好持是語。持是語者，即是持無量壽佛名。
original.edition: Taishō T12n0365 (CBETA XML P5, local copy sources_raw/cbeta), 346b12-16
original.licence: CBETA CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 (text quoted for reference)

paraphrase: Merely hearing the names of the Buddha and the two bodhisattvas removes the sins of countless kalpas, how much more recollecting them. One who recollects the Buddha is a white lotus (puṇḍarīka) among people; Avalokiteśvara and Mahāsthāmaprāpta are his friends; he will sit at the seat of awakening. The Buddha tells Ānanda: hold these words well — to hold these words is to hold the name of Amitāyus.
speaker: Śākyamuni
notes: Shandao reads this entrustment as showing that the Buddha's real intent is the calling of the name.

original.text: 韋提希與五百侍女，聞佛所說，應時即見極樂世界廣長之相，得見佛身及二菩薩。心生歡喜，歎未曾有，豁然大悟，得無生忍。
original.edition: Taishō T12n0365 (CBETA XML P5, local copy sources_raw/cbeta), 346a27-b01
original.licence: CBETA CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 (text quoted for reference)

paraphrase: Hearing this, Vaidehī and her five hundred attendants at once see the vast Land of Bliss, the Buddha's body and the two bodhisattvas; rejoicing, she is suddenly awakened and gains the acceptance of the non-arising of dharmas; the attendants arouse the aspiration for awakening and are foretold birth there.
speaker: narrator

original.text: 佛法有無量門，如世間道，有難、有易；陸道步行則苦，水道乘船則樂。菩薩道亦如是：或有勤行精進，或有以信方便易行疾至阿惟越致者。
original.edition: Taishō T26n1521 (CBETA XML P5, local copy sources_raw/cbeta), 41b02-06
original.licence: CBETA CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 (text quoted for reference)

paraphrase: Asked whether there is an easy way to reach non-retrogression quickly, the teacher first rebukes the question as fit for the weak, then says: the Buddha's teaching has countless gates; as worldly roads are hard or easy — walking overland is painful, sailing on water is pleasant — so in the bodhisattva path some advance by strenuous effort, others by the easy practice of faith as a skilful means quickly reach non-retrogression.
speaker: Nāgārjuna (as author)

original.text: 若人疾欲至， 不退轉地者，應以恭敬心， 執持稱名號。
original.edition: Taishō T26n1521 (CBETA XML P5, local copy sources_raw/cbeta), 41b13-14
original.licence: CBETA CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 (text quoted for reference)

paraphrase: Naming ten buddhas of the ten directions, the verse says: whoever wishes quickly to reach the stage of non-retrogression should with a reverent mind hold to and call their names; a bodhisattva wishing to reach non-retrogression in this body should recollect these buddhas and call their names.
speaker: Nāgārjuna (as author)

original.text: 阿彌陀佛本願如是：「若人念我——稱名、自歸，即入必定，得阿耨多羅三藐三菩提。」是故常應憶念。……人能念是佛， 無量力威德，即時入必定， 是故我常念。
original.edition: Taishō T26n1521 (CBETA XML P5, local copy sources_raw/cbeta), 43a10-12, 43a19-20
original.licence: CBETA CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 (text quoted for reference)

paraphrase: Among the many buddhas to be recollected, Amitābha's original vow is this: 'If anyone thinks of me, calls my name and takes refuge in me, he at once enters the stage of certainty and attains perfect awakening'; therefore one should always recollect him. In verses of praise the author says: one who can think of this Buddha of immeasurable power and majesty at once enters the stage of certainty; therefore I always think of him.
speaker: Nāgārjuna (as author)
notes: Correction: the verse reads 無量力威德 ('power and majesty'), not 功德 as sometimes quoted from memory.

original.text: 若人種善根， 疑則華不開，信心清淨者， 華開則見佛。
original.edition: Taishō T26n1521 (CBETA XML P5, local copy sources_raw/cbeta), 43b18-19
original.licence: CBETA CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 (text quoted for reference)

paraphrase: If one plants good roots but doubts, the lotus does not open; for one whose faith is pure, the lotus opens and he sees the Buddha.
speaker: Nāgārjuna (as author)

original.text: 世尊我一心， 歸命盡十方，無礙光如來， 願生安樂國。我依修多羅， 真實功德相，說願偈總持， 與佛教相應。
original.edition: Taishō T26n1524 (CBETA XML P5, local copy sources_raw/cbeta), 230c17-20
original.licence: CBETA CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 (text quoted for reference)

paraphrase: World-honoured One, with single mind I take refuge in the Tathāgata of Unhindered Light filling the ten directions and aspire to be born in the Land of Peace and Bliss. Relying on the sūtras and their true, virtuous marks, I set out these verses of aspiration, a summary in accord with the Buddha's teaching.
speaker: Vasubandhu
notes: Shinran reads 'single mind' (一心) as the other-power shinjin of the eighteenth vow.

original.text: 觀彼世界相， 勝過三界道，究竟如虛空， 廣大無邊際。
original.edition: Taishō T26n1524 (CBETA XML P5, local copy sources_raw/cbeta), 230c21-22
original.licence: CBETA CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 (text quoted for reference)

paraphrase: Contemplating the features of that world, it surpasses the paths of the three realms; ultimately it is like space, vast and boundless.
speaker: Vasubandhu

original.text: 大乘善根界， 等無譏嫌名，女人及根缺， 二乘種不生。
original.edition: Taishō T26n1524 (CBETA XML P5, local copy sources_raw/cbeta), 231a13-14
original.licence: CBETA CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 (text quoted for reference)

paraphrase: It is a realm of Mahāyāna good roots, all equal, without even the name of anything reproachable; women, those with deficient faculties and those of the two-vehicle kind are not born there. The prose explains that the land is free of reproach both in substance (no persons of the two vehicles, no women, no one lacking faculties) and in name (not even these names are heard), for all are equal, of one mark.
speaker: Vasubandhu
notes: Recorded faithfully. Later readers (Jingtu shiyi lun, doubt 9) read it as describing those already born, not as excluding women of this world from birth; Tiantai tradition noted a variant 男 for 界 (T1524 note).

original.text: 觀佛本願力， 遇無空過者，能令速滿足， 功德大寶海。
original.edition: Taishō T26n1524 (CBETA XML P5, local copy sources_raw/cbeta), 231a24-25
original.licence: CBETA CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 (text quoted for reference)

paraphrase: Contemplating the power of the Buddha's original vow, none who meet it pass by in vain; it swiftly fills them with the great treasure-ocean of merit. The prose adds that on seeing that Buddha, bodhisattvas who have not yet realised the pure mind finally attain the dharma-body of equality, no different from those who have.
speaker: Vasubandhu
notes: Key verse for Tanluan's and Shinran's 'power of the original vow'.

original.text: 若善男子善女人，修五念門成就者，畢竟得生安樂國土，見彼阿彌陀佛。何等五念門？一者禮拜門；二者讚歎門；三者作願門；四者觀察門；五者迴向門。
original.edition: Taishō T26n1524 (CBETA XML P5, local copy sources_raw/cbeta), 231b10-13
original.licence: CBETA CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 (text quoted for reference)

paraphrase: Whoever perfects the five gates of mindfulness will certainly be born in the Land of Peace and Bliss and see Amitābha: (1) worship — bowing to Amitābha with the body, intending birth there; (2) praise — with speech calling the Tathāgata's name, in accord with the Tathāgata's light, the mark of his wisdom, and the meaning of his name, wishing to practise in accord with reality; (3) aspiration — with the mind always aspiring single-mindedly to birth, to practise śamatha truly; (4) contemplation — with wisdom and right mindfulness contemplating the adornments of the land, the Buddha and the bodhisattvas, to practise vipaśyanā truly; (5) transfer — not abandoning any suffering being, making the transfer of merit foremost, to fulfil the mind of great compassion.
speaker: Vasubandhu

original.text: 觀察彼佛國土功德莊嚴者，有十七種事應知。……觀佛功德莊嚴成就者，有八種應知。……觀彼菩薩有四種正修行功德成就應知。
original.edition: Taishō T26n1524 (CBETA XML P5, local copy sources_raw/cbeta), 231b27-28, 232a15-16, 232b05-07
original.licence: CBETA CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 (text quoted for reference)

paraphrase: The object of contemplation is twenty-nine adornments: seventeen of the land (purity, measure, nature, form, manifold things, wondrous colour, touch, the adornments of water, ground and space, rain, light, sound, the lord, the retinue, enjoyment, freedom from difficulties, the gate of the great meaning, fulfilment of all wishes), eight of the Buddha (seat, body, speech, mind, assembly, leader, lord, sustaining power that is not in vain) and four of the bodhisattvas (unmoving yet manifesting everywhere, in one instant, making offerings everywhere, establishing the Three Jewels where they are absent).
speaker: Vasubandhu

original.text: 此三種成就願心莊嚴，略說入一法句故。一法句者，謂清淨句。清淨句者，謂真實智慧無為法身故。
original.edition: Taishō T26n1524 (CBETA XML P5, local copy sources_raw/cbeta), 232b23-25
original.licence: CBETA CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 (text quoted for reference)

paraphrase: These three kinds of accomplishment are adornments of the vow-mind; in brief they enter the one dharma-phrase, which is the pure phrase, which is the uncreated dharma-body of true wisdom. This purity is of two kinds: the purity of the vessel-world (the seventeen adornments of the land) and the purity of the world of beings (the adornments of the Buddha and bodhisattvas).
speaker: Vasubandhu

original.text: 謂說禮拜等五種修行所集一切功德善根，不求自身住持之樂，欲拔一切眾生苦故，作願攝取一切眾生，共同生彼安樂佛國。
original.edition: Taishō T26n1524 (CBETA XML P5, local copy sources_raw/cbeta), 232c05-09
original.licence: CBETA CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 (text quoted for reference)

paraphrase: By broad and brief practice of śamatha and vipaśyanā the bodhisattva gains a pliant mind and skilful transfer: he does not seek his own pleasure with the merit gathered by the five practices but vows to take in all beings and be born together with them in that land. He thus leaves the three things contrary to awakening (attachment to self, not giving beings peace, seeking honour for himself) through the gates of wisdom, compassion and skilful means, and fulfils the three pure minds that accord with awakening.
speaker: Vasubandhu

original.text: 出第五門，以大慈悲觀察一切苦惱眾生，亦應化身迴入生死園煩惱林中，遊戲神通至教化地，以本願力迴向故，是名出第五門。
original.edition: Taishō T26n1524 (CBETA XML P5, local copy sources_raw/cbeta), 233a19-22
original.licence: CBETA CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 (text quoted for reference)

paraphrase: Five gates of merit are gradually accomplished: by worship one enters the first gate (approach), born in the Land of Peace and Bliss; by praise and calling the name, the second (joining the great assembly); by single-minded aspiration and the tranquil samādhi of śamatha, the third (the dwelling: the lotus-store world); by vipaśyanā, the fourth (the chamber: enjoying the flavours of the dharma). The first four are gates of entering, of benefiting oneself; by the fifth, going out, one looks with great compassion on suffering beings, manifests transformation bodies and re-enters the garden of birth-and-death and the forest of passions, playing with superknowledges at the stage of teaching, by the power of the original vow. Thus benefiting self and others the bodhisattva swiftly attains perfect awakening.
speaker: Vasubandhu

location.section: T945 fasc. 5, Mahāsthāmaprāpta's perfect penetration through recollecting the Buddha

paraphrase: Mahāsthāmaprāpta tells how he entered samādhi by recollecting the Buddha: as a mother remembers her child, if beings remember the Buddha they will surely see him now or later; gathering in all six faculties, with pure recollection continuing moment after moment, he attained samādhi — for him the best of the penetrations — and he now receives recollecting beings into the Pure Land.
speaker: Mahāsthāmaprāpta
notes: T19 not in local corpus; wording recalled, no original. Chapter added to the Pure Land canon by Yinguang.

paraphrase: At the close of Samantabhadra's vows the practitioner aspires: at the moment of death, may all obstacles be removed, may I see Amitābha face to face and be born at once in Sukhāvatī, and there fulfil these vows and benefit all beings.
speaker: Samantabhadra
notes: Not read locally; verse numbers approximate (low).

paraphrase: Tanluan begins from Nāgārjuna: a bodhisattva seeking non-retrogression in an age of the five turbidities and without a buddha finds two paths, the difficult and the easy. The difficult is like walking overland — outsiders' seeming good confuses, śrāvakas' self-benefit obstructs great compassion, evil people destroy others' merit, results obtained by delusion ruin pure practice, and there is only self-power without support from other-power. The easy path is simply to aspire to birth in the Pure Land through faith in the Buddha; riding on the power of the Buddha's vow one is born there, and upheld by the Buddha's power one enters the rightly established group of the Mahāyāna — like sailing on water.
speaker: Tanluan
notes: T40n1819 not in local corpus; recalled without original (fascicle-level ref).

location.section: fasc. 2, on the gate of praise

paraphrase: Commenting on 'calling that Tathāgata's name in accord with ... the meaning of the name, wishing to practise in accord with reality': the name of the Tathāgata of Unhindered Light can break all the ignorance of beings and fulfil all their aspirations; yet some call the name and ignorance remains because they do not practise in accord with reality, not knowing that the Tathāgata is the body of reality and the body for beings; and because of three kinds of non-accord: faith that is not genuine, faith that is not single, and faith that is not continuous. The three mutually entail one another; their opposites are the three faiths.
speaker: Tanluan
notes: T40n1819 not in local corpus; recalled without original (fascicle-level ref).

location.section: end of fasc. 1, eight questions and answers

paraphrase: In eight questions Tanluan asks who is born: the Larger Sūtra excludes those guilty of the five grave offences and slander of the Dharma, while the Contemplation Sūtra lets even five-offence evil-doers be born by ten recitations; he answers that one guilty of both offences and slander cannot be born, one who has only committed the grave offences but not slandered can be; slander is the gravest since it rejects the very Dharma; the ten continuous recitations outweigh a lifetime's evil because their weight lies in the mind, the object and decisiveness, not in length of time; 'ten recitations' need not be counted — one simply continues without other thoughts; the count is known to the sages.
speaker: Tanluan
notes: T40n1819 not in local corpus; recalled without original (fascicle-level ref). Daochuo quotes the core argument verbatim (Anle ji 10c-11a, read locally).

location.section: fasc. 2, on the entering of the adornments into the one phrase

paraphrase: All buddhas and bodhisattvas have two dharma-bodies: the dharma-body of dharma-nature and the dharma-body of expedient means. From the dharma-body of dharma-nature arises the dharma-body of expedient means, and through the dharma-body of expedient means the dharma-body of dharma-nature is manifested; the two are different but cannot be separated, one but cannot be identified. Therefore the broad (twenty-nine adornments) and the brief (the one dharma-phrase) enter into each other.
speaker: Tanluan
notes: T40n1819 not in local corpus; recalled without original (fascicle-level ref).

paraphrase: To the objection that seeking birth contradicts the Mahāyāna teaching of non-arising, Tanluan answers that birth in that land is the 'birth of non-birth' arising from Amitābha's pure original vow, not the deluded birth of the three existences; even one of lower grade who calls the name without knowing this, once born there, finds the attachment to birth dissolved — as ice placed on fire melts and the fire goes out.
speaker: Tanluan
notes: T40n1819 not in local corpus; recalled without original (fascicle-level ref). The phrase 無生之生 is read locally in Daochuo's quotation.

location.section: fasc. 2, on the gate of transfer

paraphrase: Transfer of merit has two aspects: in the going aspect one transfers one's merit to all beings, vowing to be born together with them in Amitābha's land; in the returning aspect, having been born there and attained śamatha and vipaśyanā and the power of skilful means, one returns to the dense forest of birth-and-death to teach all beings and turn them to the Buddha's path.
speaker: Tanluan
notes: T40n1819 not in local corpus; recalled without original (fascicle-level ref).

paraphrase: In all three grades of the Larger Sūtra the aspirants arouse the unsurpassed aspiration for awakening; this aspiration is the mind that vows to become a buddha, which is the mind that vows to save beings, which is the mind that takes beings in and brings them to be born in a buddha-land. One who aspires to birth only for the endless pleasures there will not be born.
speaker: Tanluan
notes: T40n1819 not in local corpus; recalled without original (fascicle-level ref).

paraphrase: Seeking the root of it all, Amitābha is the dominant condition: birth there, the activity of the bodhisattvas and humans and gods there all arise from the power of his original vow. As proof, the eighteenth vow makes birth possible through ten recitations, the eleventh ensures that those born dwell in the rightly established group and so avoid retrogression, the twenty-second lets them surpass the ordinary stages and practise Samantabhadra's virtue. By this, other-power is the dominant condition. As an inferior man who cannot mount a donkey by himself can travel through space by joining the retinue of a wheel-turning king, so beings ride the Buddha's power; students should not think only of self-power.
speaker: Tanluan
notes: T40n1819 not in local corpus; recalled without original (fascicle-level ref). The donkey / wheel-turning king simile recalled in outline.

original.text: 如斯淨土，非三界所攝。何以故？無欲故，非欲界；地居故，非色界；有形色故，非無色界。
original.edition: Taishō T47n1957 (CBETA XML P5, local copy sources_raw/cbeta), 1a06-08
original.licence: CBETA CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 (text quoted for reference)

paraphrase: Asked which of the three realms includes the Land of Peace and Bliss: as the (Mahāprajñāpāramitā) treatise says, such a pure land is not included in the three realms — not the desire realm, being without desire; not the form realm, being on the ground; not the formless realm, having form; it was gained by Dharmākara's special karma through vows and the perfections over countless kalpas.
speaker: Tanluan (attrib.)

original.text: 安樂國土謂之邊地，亦曰胎生。邊地者，言其五百歲中不見聞三寶，義同邊地之難；……胎生者，譬如胎生人初生之時，人法未成。邊言其難，胎言其闇
original.edition: Taishō T47n1957 (CBETA XML P5, local copy sources_raw/cbeta), 2a07-10
original.licence: CBETA CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 (text quoted for reference)

paraphrase: Besides the three grades there is a kind of birth for those who cultivate merit with a doubting mind, not understanding the Buddha's inconceivable wisdom; they dwell in jewelled palaces, happy as in the Trāyastriṃśa heaven, but for five hundred years do not see the Buddha or hear the Dharma. This is called the borderland (its difficulty) and womb-birth (its darkness) — names borrowed by analogy, for all in that land are born by transformation and after five hundred years they see and hear the Three Jewels.
speaker: Tanluan (attrib.)

original.text: 不思議智者，謂佛智力能以少作多，以多作少；以近為遠，以遠為近；以輕為重，以重為輕……譬如百夫、百年聚薪，積高千仞，豆許火焚，半日便盡。……又如躄者寄載他船，因風帆勢，一日至千里。
original.edition: Taishō T47n1957 (CBETA XML P5, local copy sources_raw/cbeta), 2b10-16
original.licence: CBETA CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 (text quoted for reference)

paraphrase: To the doubt how ten continuous recitations can outweigh a lifetime of evil and take one out of the three realms without cutting the fetters, the answer is the Buddha's inconceivable wisdom, which can make little much and much little, the heavy light and the light heavy: a hundred years of firewood piled by a hundred men is burned in half a day by a bean-sized fire; a lame man carried on another's ship with the wind reaches a thousand li in a day.
speaker: Tanluan (attrib.)

original.text: 現在西方去此界，十萬億剎安樂土，佛世尊號阿彌陀，我願往生歸命禮。……智慧光明不可量，故佛又號無量光，有量諸相蒙光曉，是故稽首真實明。
original.edition: Taishō T47n1978 (CBETA XML P5, local copy sources_raw/cbeta), 420c18-19, 420c26-27
original.licence: CBETA CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 (text quoted for reference)

paraphrase: Tanluan's hymn: in the West, ten trillion lands from here, is the Land of Peace and Bliss whose Buddha is Amitābha; he became a buddha ten kalpas ago and his life is immeasurable; his dharma-body's wheel of light pervades the dharma-realm; for his wisdom-light he is called Immeasurable Light, Boundless Light, Unhindered Light, Incomparable Light (and so on through twelve names); those touched by his light are freed of being and non-being, their karmic bonds removed. Each verse ends: may I with all beings be born in the Land of Peace and Bliss.
speaker: Tanluan

original.text: 若教赴時機，易修易悟；若機教時乖，難修難入。
original.edition: Taishō T47n1958 (CBETA XML P5, local copy sources_raw/cbeta), 4a26-27
original.licence: CBETA CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 (text quoted for reference)

paraphrase: The first great gate: teaching arises according to the time and the capacity of beings. If the teaching fits the time and the capacity, it is easy to practise and easy to awaken; if capacity, teaching and time are at odds, it is hard to practise and hard to enter — like drilling wet wood for fire.
speaker: Daochuo

original.text: 計今時眾生，即當佛去世後第四五百年，正是懺悔、修福，應稱佛名號時者。若一念稱阿彌陀佛，即能除却八十億劫生死之罪。
original.edition: Taishō T47n1958 (CBETA XML P5, local copy sources_raw/cbeta), 4b16-19
original.licence: CBETA CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 (text quoted for reference)

paraphrase: Citing the Candragarbha (Mahāsaṃnipāta) sūtra's five periods of five hundred years after the Buddha — wisdom, concentration, learning, building stūpas and repentance, then disputes — Daochuo reckons that beings now are in the fourth five hundred years, the time for repentance, merit and calling the Buddha's name; one calling of Amitābha removes the sins of eighty koṭis of kalpas of birth-and-death. When the sage was near, meditation and wisdom were the main practice and calling the name secondary; now that the sage is far, calling the name is main and the others secondary.
speaker: Daochuo

location.section: T1958 fasc. 1, first great gate, fourth item

original.text: 今此《觀經》以觀佛三昧為宗。
original.edition: Taishō T47n1958 (CBETA XML P5, local copy sources_raw/cbeta), 5a (fourth item of the first gate)
original.licence: CBETA CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 (text quoted for reference)

paraphrase: Different sūtras have different themes — the Nirvāṇa buddha-nature, the Vimalakīrti inconceivable liberation, the Prajñāpāramitā empty wisdom, the Mahāsaṃnipāta dhāraṇī; the Contemplation Sūtra has the samādhi of contemplating the Buddha as its theme.
speaker: Daochuo
notes: Line within 5a not isolated.

original.text: 此念佛三昧即是一切三昧中王故也。
original.edition: Taishō T47n1958 (CBETA XML P5, local copy sources_raw/cbeta), 5c09-10
original.licence: CBETA CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 (text quoted for reference)

paraphrase: Practising the nianfo samādhi within the aspiration for awakening, all demons and obstacles are passed without difficulty, like a drop of lion's milk that dissolves all other milk; for this samādhi of recollecting the Buddha is the king among all samādhis.
speaker: Daochuo

location.section: T1958 fasc. 1, seventh item of the first gate

original.text: 現在彌陀是報佛，極樂寶莊嚴國是報土。然古舊相傳皆云：『阿彌陀佛是化身，土亦是化土。』此為大失也。
original.edition: Taishō T47n1958 (CBETA XML P5, local copy sources_raw/cbeta), 5c12-15
original.licence: CBETA CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 (text quoted for reference)

paraphrase: Asked what body the present Amitābha is and what land Sukhāvatī is, Daochuo answers: Amitābha now is a reward-body buddha and the jewel-adorned Land of Bliss is a reward land; the old tradition that he is a transformation body in a transformation land is a great error — for then where would the reward body dwell? Citing a sūtra, all who become buddhas in pure lands are reward bodies, those in defiled lands transformation bodies.
speaker: Daochuo

location.section: T1958 fasc. 1, ninth item of the first gate

original.text: 淨土勝妙，體出世間。此三界者，乃是生死凡夫之闇宅……是故淨土非三界攝。
original.edition: Taishō T47n1958 (CBETA XML P5, local copy sources_raw/cbeta), 7a26-b02
original.licence: CBETA CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 (text quoted for reference)

paraphrase: The Pure Land is excellent and wondrous, in substance beyond the world; the three realms are the dark house of ordinary beings in birth-and-death, a long river of defilement where cause and effect breed falsehood, deeply to be loathed; therefore the Pure Land is not included in the three realms.
speaker: Daochuo

location.section: T1958 fasc. 1, third great gate? (comparison with Tuṣita)

original.text: 願生兜率，不願歸西。……此義不類，少分似同，據體大別，有其四種。
original.edition: Taishō T47n1958 (CBETA XML P5, local copy sources_raw/cbeta), 9b23-25
original.licence: CBETA CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 (text quoted for reference)

paraphrase: To those who prefer birth in Maitreya's Tuṣita to the West, Daochuo answers that they are only slightly alike and fundamentally different in four ways: in Tuṣita many are attached to pleasure and retrogress; life there is four thousand years and then one falls; its birds and trees serve the gods' sensual pleasure and do not aid the holy path, while in the Pure Land all are non-retrogressive, beyond the three realms, of life equal to the Buddha's, and even its birds and trees preach the Dharma.
speaker: Daochuo
notes: Section heading reads 第七、會通願生兜率勸歸淨土 (within the second great gate); great-gate number not verified.

original.text: 今此經中但說一生造罪，臨命終時十念成就即得往生。不論過去有因、無因者，直是世尊引接當來造惡之徒，令其臨終捨惡歸善，乘念往生，是以隱其宿因。
original.edition: Taishō T47n1958 (CBETA XML P5, local copy sources_raw/cbeta), 10a19-22
original.licence: CBETA CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 (text quoted for reference)

paraphrase: Against teachers of the Mahāyānasaṃgraha who called the Contemplation Sūtra's promise of birth by ten recitations an 'intention for another time' (only a cause for a distant future birth, as one coin buys a thousand only in time), Daochuo holds that a treatise may not contradict the sūtra: the Buddha, leading future evil-doers, hides their past causes and speaks only of the result; those who complete the ten recitations all have past causes, as the Nirvāṇa Sūtra shows, and so are born at once.
speaker: Daochuo

original.text: 正明在心、在緣、在決定，不在時節久近、多少也。
original.edition: Taishō T47n1958 (CBETA XML P5, local copy sources_raw/cbeta), 10c22
original.licence: CBETA CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 (text quoted for reference)

paraphrase: To the objection that karma is like a scale where the heavier side pulls first, so how can ten recitations at death outweigh a lifetime of evil: the weight lies in the mind, the object and decisiveness, not in length of time. In the mind: the evil arose from a false, inverted mind; the ten recitations arise from hearing the Dharma of reality through a good teacher's skilful comfort — one real, one false; as light entering a room dark for a thousand years dispels the dark at once.
speaker: Daochuo (after Tanluan)

original.text: 但憶念阿彌陀佛，若總相、若別相，隨所緣觀，逕於十念，無他念想間雜，是名十念。又云：『十念相續者，是聖者一數之名耳。』但能積念凝思，不緣他事，使業道成辦，便罷不用，亦未勞記之頭數也。又云：『若久行人念，多應依此；若始行人念者，記數亦好。』
original.edition: Taishō T47n1958 (CBETA XML P5, local copy sources_raw/cbeta), 11a21-27
original.licence: CBETA CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 (text quoted for reference)

paraphrase: How long is 'ten recitations'? Not the scriptural measure of moments: simply recollecting Amitābha, by his general or particular marks as one contemplates, through ten thoughts without other thoughts intervening is called ten recitations. 'Ten' is a number known to the sages; one only accumulates recollection without other concerns until the karmic path is complete, without troubling to count; practitioners of long standing may do so, while beginners may well count.
speaker: Daochuo (quoting Tanluan)

original.text: 各宜同志三、五預結言要，臨命終時，迭相開曉，為稱彌陀名號，願生安樂國，聲聲相次，使成十念也。譬如蠟印印泥，印壞文成。此命斷時，即是生安樂國時。
original.edition: Taishō T47n1958 (CBETA XML P5, local copy sources_raw/cbeta), 11b24-28
original.licence: CBETA CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 (text quoted for reference)

paraphrase: Do not put off practice to the deathbed: ordinary minds are like wild horses and monkeys; build the habit now, for when the 'wind-knife' of death comes with a hundred pains the recitation cannot be managed if it was not practised. Let three or five like-minded people make a pact in advance: at the time of death they take turns reminding the dying one and calling Amitābha's name, voice following voice, so that the ten recitations are completed — as a wax seal pressed in clay: when the seal breaks the pattern is formed; the moment life ends is the moment of birth in the Land of Peace and Bliss.
speaker: Daochuo

original.text: 然彼淨土乃是阿彌陀如來清淨本願，無生之生。非如三有眾生愛染，虛妄執著生也。何以故？夫法性清淨畢竟無生，而言生者，得生者之情耳。
original.edition: Taishō T47n1958 (CBETA XML P5, local copy sources_raw/cbeta), 11c11-14
original.licence: CBETA CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 (text quoted for reference)

paraphrase: If birth is the root of all troubles, is not seeking birth in the Pure Land abandoning birth only to seek birth? No: that land is the birth of non-birth from Amitābha's pure original vow, not the deluded, attached birth of beings in the three existences; dharma-nature is pure and ultimately unborn — 'birth' is said only from the standpoint of those who are born. (Earlier: 'beings are ultimately unborn like space' is true, and birth by conditions is nominal birth, hence non-birth.)
speaker: Daochuo (after Tanluan)

original.text: 何者為二？一謂聖道；二謂往生淨土。其聖道一種今時難證。一、由去大聖遙遠；二、由理深解微。……當今末法，現是五濁惡世，唯有淨土一門，可通入路。
original.edition: Taishō T47n1958 (CBETA XML P5, local copy sources_raw/cbeta), 13c06-11
original.licence: CBETA CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 (text quoted for reference)

paraphrase: Why do beings who all have buddha-nature and have met many buddhas still transmigrate? Because they have not taken either of two excellent dharmas: the holy path and birth in the Pure Land. The holy path is hard to realise now, because the great sage is long gone and its principle is deep while understanding is shallow; the Candragarbha says that in the last age not one of countless practitioners attains. Now in the last age, this evil world of five turbidities, only the gate of the Pure Land is passable. The Larger Sūtra says even one who has done evil all his life, if at death he calls the name ten times continuously, will be born. Even a lifetime's evil-doer who fixes his mind and recollects the Buddha will have all obstacles removed and be born.
speaker: Daochuo
notes: Daochuo's wording of the vow ('縱令一生造惡 ... 十念相續稱我名字') differs from T360 and follows the Contemplation Sūtra; Hōnen's Senchakushū ch. 1 opens with this passage.

original.text: 問曰：今欲勸人往生者，未知若為安心起行作業定得往生彼國土也？答曰：必欲生彼國土者，如《觀經》說者，具三心必得往生。……二者深心，即是真實信心，信知自身是具足煩惱凡夫、善根薄少，流轉三界、不出火宅。今信知彌陀本弘誓願及稱名號，下至十聲一聲等定得往生，乃至一念無有疑心，故名深心。
original.edition: Taishō T47n1980 (CBETA XML P5, local copy sources_raw/cbeta), 438c01-10
original.licence: CBETA CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 (text quoted for reference)

paraphrase: How should one settle the mind, undertake practice and carry it out so as surely to be born? By the three minds of the Contemplation Sūtra: the sincere mind — true in the three acts of worship, praise and contemplation; the deep mind — true entrusting, knowing oneself to be an ordinary being full of passions, with scant roots of good, transmigrating in the three realms and not leaving the burning house, and knowing that by Amitābha's original universal vow and the calling of his name, down to ten or even one calling, one will surely be born, without a single thought of doubt; and the mind that dedicates merit and aspires to birth. With these three one is surely born; lacking one, one is not.
speaker: Shandao

location.section: T1980 preface, four modes of practice

original.text: 一者恭敬修，所謂恭敬禮拜彼佛及彼一切聖眾等，故名恭敬修。……二者無餘修，所謂專稱彼佛名，專念專想專禮專讚彼佛及一切聖眾等，不雜餘業，故名無餘修。……三者無間修，所謂相續恭敬禮拜、稱名讚歎、憶念觀察、回向發願，心心相續不以餘業來間，故名無間修。
original.edition: Taishō T47n1980 (CBETA XML P5, local copy sources_raw/cbeta), 439a08-15
original.licence: CBETA CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 (text quoted for reference)

paraphrase: Four modes of practice spur the three minds: reverent practice (worshipping that Buddha and the holy ones); exclusive practice (only calling that Buddha's name, recollecting, worshipping and praising him, mixing in no other practice); uninterrupted practice (continuing without other practices or passions intervening, repenting at once when one lapses); and each 'until the end of life, vowing never to stop', which is the long-lasting practice.
speaker: Shandao

original.text: 問曰：何故不令作觀，直遣專稱名字者，有何意也？答曰：乃由眾生障重，境細心麁、識颺神飛，觀難成就也。是以大聖悲憐，直勸專稱名字。正由稱名易故，相續即生。
original.edition: Taishō T47n1980 (CBETA XML P5, local copy sources_raw/cbeta), 439a27-b01
original.licence: CBETA CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 (text quoted for reference)

paraphrase: Citing the Mañjuśrī Prajñāpāramitā's single-practice samādhi (dwell alone, fix the mind on one buddha, do not contemplate his features, only call his name): why not contemplation, but only calling the name? Because beings' hindrances are heavy, the object is subtle while the mind is coarse, consciousness flies and spirit scatters, and contemplation is hard to achieve; the great sage in compassion directly urged exclusive calling of the name; because calling is easy, continuing it one is born.
speaker: Shandao

original.text: 若能如上念念相續、畢命為期者，十即十生、百即百生。……若欲捨專修雜業者，百時希得一二、千時希得三五。……但使專意作者，十即十生；修雜不至心者，千中無一。
original.edition: Taishō T47n1980 (CBETA XML P5, local copy sources_raw/cbeta), 439b17-21, 439c01-02
original.licence: CBETA CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 (text quoted for reference)

paraphrase: If one continues moment after moment until the end of life, ten of ten are born, a hundred of a hundred — for no outside conditions disturb right mindfulness, it accords with the Buddha's vow, the teaching and the Buddha's words. If one abandons exclusive practice for mixed practices, hardly one or two in a hundred, three or five in a thousand are born — because mixed conditions disturb right mindfulness, it does not accord with the vow, recollection is not continuous, the dedication is not earnest, passions interrupt, there is no shame or repentance, no thought of repaying the Buddha's kindness, pride and pursuit of fame and gain, no reliance on good companions. Whoever practises wholeheartedly, ten of ten are born; of mixed and insincere practice, not one in a thousand.
speaker: Shandao

original.text: 又如《無量壽經》云：若我成佛，十方眾生稱我名號，下至十聲，若不生者，不取正覺。彼佛今現在世成佛，當知本誓重願不虛，眾生稱念必得往生。
original.edition: Taishō T47n1980 (CBETA XML P5, local copy sources_raw/cbeta), 447c23-26
original.licence: CBETA CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 (text quoted for reference)

paraphrase: Shandao paraphrases the eighteenth vow as: 'If, when I become a buddha, beings of the ten directions who call my name even down to ten voicings are not born, may I not attain perfect awakening'; that Buddha has now become a buddha in the world, so know that the grave original vow is not in vain: beings who call and recollect will surely be born.
speaker: Shandao
notes: T1980 reads 彼佛今現在世成佛; the Japanese quotations (Senchakushū, Kyōgyōshinshō) are usually given as 彼佛今現在成佛. Shandao's reading of 十念 as 十聲 (ten voicings) is decisive for Hōnen.

original.text: 七日之中皆須一食長齋……於道場中晝夜束心相續，專心念阿彌陀佛，心與聲相續。……所見境界不得輒說，善者自知，惡者懺悔。
original.edition: Taishō T47n1959 (CBETA XML P5, local copy sources_raw/cbeta), 24b04-16
original.licence: CBETA CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 (text quoted for reference)

paraphrase: Entering the samādhi hall: prepare a clean room with an image on the west wall; at one of four fixed times of the month, according to one's household duties, enter for one to seven days in clean clothes, taking one vegetarian meal a day; day and night bind the mind in continuous recollection of Amitābha, mind and voice together, standing or sitting, not sleeping, not whispering to others; confess the sins of this life at the three or six periods; visions that appear should not be told lightly — good ones are known to oneself, bad ones should be repented; vow off wine, meat and the five pungent roots.
speaker: Shandao
notes: The text itself prescribes seven days without sleep; recorded as the text's instruction, not as advice.

original.text: 又行者等若病不病欲命終時，一依上念佛三昧法正當身心，迴面向西，心亦專注觀想阿彌陀佛。心口相應聲聲莫絕，決定作往生想、華臺聖眾來迎接想。病人若見前境，即向看病人說。
original.edition: Taishō T47n1959 (CBETA XML P5, local copy sources_raw/cbeta), 24b21-25
original.licence: CBETA CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 (text quoted for reference)

paraphrase: When a practitioner, ill or not, is about to die, let him follow the samādhi method: set body and mind right, face west, fix the mind on contemplating Amitābha, mind and voice in accord without a break, with the conviction of birth and the thought of the lotus-dais and holy ones coming to welcome him. If he sees visions he tells his attendant, who records them; if he cannot speak the attendant keeps asking what he sees; if he tells of signs of sin, those beside him recite and repent with him until the sin is removed and the lotus-dais appears. Relatives who have taken wine, meat or pungent roots must not approach the sick one, lest he lose right mindfulness, be troubled by spirits, die deranged and fall into the evil paths.
speaker: Shandao

original.text: 一者滅罪增上緣。二者護念得長命增上緣。三者見佛增上緣。四者攝生增上緣。五者證生增上緣。
original.edition: Taishō T47n1959 (CBETA XML P5, local copy sources_raw/cbeta), 24c20-22
original.licence: CBETA CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 (text quoted for reference)

paraphrase: Those who call Amitābha's name aspiring to the Pure Land gain, in this life and after, five augmenting conditions: the extinction of sins; protection and long life; seeing the Buddha (by the three powers of the Buddha's vow, the samādhi and one's own merit, after the Pratyutpanna); being embraced; and the testimony of the buddhas that one will be born.
speaker: Shandao

paraphrase: Shandao 'settles the old and the new': the Buddha and land are reward, not transformation, since they arise from Dharmākara's vows and practice; though a reward land is lofty, ordinary beings full of defilements can enter it because they ride on the power of the Buddha's vow as the augmenting condition; and all nine grades of the sūtra are ordinary beings who have met evil or good conditions, not sages of the stages, against masters who ranked the upper grades as bodhisattvas.
speaker: Shandao
notes: T37n1753 not in local corpus; recalled, no original.

paraphrase: The sūtra has two gates: the essential gate (yaomen) — Śākyamuni's teaching of the meditative and non-meditative good dedicated to birth — and the universal vow (hongyuan), Amitābha's vow by whose power all good and evil ordinary beings are born.
speaker: Shandao
notes: T37n1753 not in local corpus; recalled, no original.

paraphrase: The sincere mind means that practice of body, speech and mind must be done with a true mind: one should not outwardly show signs of wisdom, goodness and diligence while inwardly harbouring falsehood; practice mixed with greed, anger and deceit, even done with urgency as if brushing fire from one's head, is 'poisoned good', unfit for birth in the land built by the Buddha's true mind.
speaker: Shandao
notes: T37n1753 not in local corpus; recalled, no original. Shinran reads the key line differently ('do not show outwardly ... for inwardly one harbours falsehood').

paraphrase: The deep mind is deeply entrusting mind, of two kinds: first, to believe deeply and decisively that one is now a foolish ordinary being of sin and evil in birth-and-death, ever sinking and ever flowing since countless kalpas, without any condition for escape; second, to believe deeply and decisively that Amitābha's forty-eight vows embrace beings and that, without doubt or anxiety, riding the power of his vow one will surely be born.
speaker: Shandao
notes: T37n1753 not in local corpus; recalled, no original.

location.section: fasc. 4 (Sanshan yi), deep mind: establishing faith through practice

paraphrase: Practices are of two kinds, right and miscellaneous. The right practices are five, all directed to Amitābha: reading and reciting the Pure Land sūtras, contemplating that land and Buddha, worshipping him, calling his name, and praising and making offerings. Of these, to single-mindedly recollect Amitābha's name, whether walking, standing, sitting or lying, without regard to the length of time, never abandoning it moment to moment — this is called the rightly determined act, because it accords with that Buddha's vow; the others are auxiliary acts. All other good practices are called miscellaneous.
speaker: Shandao
notes: T37n1753 not in local corpus; recalled, no original. The line (一心專念彌陀名號 ... 是名正定之業，順彼佛願故) converted Hōnen in 1175.

location.section: fasc. 4 (Sanshan yi), the parable of the two rivers

paraphrase: A traveller going west across a wilderness, pursued by bandits and wild beasts, meets two rivers — fire to the south, water to the north — each a hundred paces wide and bottomless, with a white path only four or five inches wide between them, lashed by waves and flames. From the eastern bank a voice urges him to go resolutely; from the western bank a voice calls him to come straight on without fear. Bandits call him back, saying the path is dangerous; he goes on single-mindedly and reaches the western bank, free of all dangers, meeting good friends. The east bank is this burning house, the west the Pure Land; the bandits and beasts are the six senses, consciousnesses and elements, and those of differing views; the water is greed, the fire anger; the white path is the pure aspiration for birth arising amid passions; the voice from the east is Śākyamuni's exhortation, from the west Amitābha's call.
speaker: Shandao
notes: T37n1753 not in local corpus; recalled, no original.

location.section: fasc. 4 (Sanshan yi), on the lower-lower grade

paraphrase: Why does the eighteenth vow exclude the five grave offences and slander while the Contemplation Sūtra admits five-offence evil-doers? The vow's exclusion is the gate of restraint (yizhi men): the Buddha, fearing that beings would commit these two gravest faults and fall into hell for long ages, speaks of exclusion to restrain them; it does not mean they are not embraced. Once committed, they too are taken in and born — though those so born remain in closed lotuses for many kalpas.
speaker: Shandao
notes: T37n1753 not in local corpus; recalled, no original.

location.section: fasc. 4, on the entrustment to Ānanda

paraphrase: Although the sūtra has taught the benefits of meditative and non-meditative good, when one looks to the Buddha's original vow its intent is that beings single-mindedly and exclusively call Amitābha's name.
speaker: Shandao
notes: T37n1753 not in local corpus; recalled, no original.

paraphrase: Shandao writes that before composing the commentary he vowed to seek a sign; each night in dreams a monk instructed him on the arrangement of the essential meaning, and after completing it he had further visions; he therefore asks that the work be treated as if it were a sūtra, not to be added to or subtracted from.
speaker: Shandao
notes: T37n1753 not in local corpus; recalled, no original. Details of the dreams recalled only in outline.

original.text: 論言「唯由發願」者，是簡持義。簡去念佛之行，持取唯空發願，更無有行。……今時念佛至心，即意業善行也；稱佛名號，即語業善行也；合掌禮拜，即身業善行也。
original.edition: Taishō T47n1960 (CBETA XML P5, local copy sources_raw/cbeta), 39a08-14
original.licence: CBETA CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 (text quoted for reference)

paraphrase: To the objection that the Mahāyānasaṃgraha calls birth 'by vow alone' an intention for another time: 'by vow alone' means a bare vow with no practice, which indeed brings birth only at another time; but present recollection with a sincere mind is good mental action, calling the name good verbal action and joining palms and worshipping good bodily action — with these three good actions one is born at once.
speaker: Huaigan

original.text: 雜修之者，萬不一生；專修之人，千無一失。
original.edition: Taishō T47n1960 (CBETA XML P5, local copy sources_raw/cbeta), 50c17
original.licence: CBETA CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 (text quoted for reference)

paraphrase: The *Pusa chutai jing* says that west of here lies a land of sloth and pride (xieman guo), pleasant and full of music, where of millions who set out for Amitābha's land only one reaches it. Huaigan explains: this is why Shandao urged exclusive practice; those of mixed practice, whose resolve is not firm, fall into the land of sloth; of mixed practitioners not one in ten thousand is born, of exclusive practitioners not one in a thousand fails.
speaker: Huaigan

original.text: 故《大集日藏分》經言「大念見大佛，小念見小佛。」大念者，大聲稱佛也。小念者，小聲稱佛也。……現見即今諸修學者，唯須勵聲念佛，三昧易成。小聲稱佛，遂多馳散。
original.edition: Taishō T47n1960 (CBETA XML P5, local copy sources_raw/cbeta), 76c01-05
original.licence: CBETA CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 (text quoted for reference)

paraphrase: Reciting aloud without break one attains samādhi and sees the Buddha and holy assembly clearly before one's eyes; the Sūryagarbha says 'great recollection sees a great buddha, small recollection a small buddha' — great means loud calling, small means soft; practitioners today find that with vigorous voiced recitation samādhi is easily achieved, while soft recitation lets the mind scatter. Try it rather than doubt.
speaker: Huaigan

original.text: 具縛凡夫，有大悲心願生惡世，救苦眾生者，無有是處。
original.edition: Taishō T47n1961 (CBETA XML P5, local copy sources_raw/cbeta), 77c03-04 (quoting the Dazhidu lun)
original.licence: CBETA CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 (text quoted for reference)

paraphrase: First doubt: bodhisattvas' task is great compassion, so should they not vow to be born in the three realms to save beings, rather than seek the Pure Land's ease? Answer: bodhisattvas who have gained the acceptance of non-arising should indeed do so; but beginners and ordinary beings must first stay near the Buddha until their power of acceptance is complete — 'that an ordinary being in bondage with great compassion should vow to be born in the evil world to save beings is impossible' — like a child who must not leave its mother, or a bird with unfledged wings.
speaker: (attrib.) Zhiyi

original.text: 智者熾然求生淨土，達生體不可得，即是真無生，此謂心淨故即佛土淨。愚者為生所縛，聞生即作生解，聞無生即作無生解，不知生者即是無生，無生即是生。
original.edition: Taishō T47n1961 (CBETA XML P5, local copy sources_raw/cbeta), 78a26-29
original.licence: CBETA CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 (text quoted for reference)

paraphrase: Second doubt: if all dharmas are empty and unborn, is seeking birth in the West not contrary to principle, and does the sūtra not say 'as the mind is pure the land is pure'? Answer: to cling to staying here is as much a fault as clinging to going there, and to seek neither is annihilationism. The buddhas teach by the two truths without destroying provisional names. The wise ardently seek birth in the Pure Land while understanding that the nature of birth cannot be found — this is true non-arising, and this is 'the mind being pure, the buddha-land is pure'; the foolish, bound by birth, take 'birth' and 'non-birth' literally, not knowing that birth is non-birth and non-birth is birth.
speaker: (attrib.) Zhiyi

original.text: 得生彼國，有五因緣不退。云何為五？一者、阿彌陀佛大悲願力攝持，故得不退；二者、佛光常照，故菩提心常增進不退；三者、水鳥、樹林，風聲、樂響，皆說苦、空……四者、彼國純諸菩薩以為良友……五者、生彼國即壽命永劫，共菩薩、佛齊等，故不退也。
original.edition: Taishō T47n1961 (CBETA XML P5, local copy sources_raw/cbeta), 79b04-14
original.licence: CBETA CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 (text quoted for reference)

paraphrase: How can ordinary beings in bondage be non-retrogressive once born? For five reasons: Amitābha's compassionate vow holds them; the Buddha's light always shines on them so the aspiration for awakening grows; the waters, birds, trees and music all preach suffering and emptiness and move them to recollect the Three Jewels; their companions are only bodhisattvas, with no evil conditions outside and no passions arising within; and their life there is as long as that of the bodhisattvas and buddhas.
speaker: (attrib.) Zhiyi

original.text: 求生兜率，一日聞道見佛，勢欲相似，若細比校，大有優、劣。
original.edition: Taishō T47n1961 (CBETA XML P5, local copy sources_raw/cbeta), 79b19-21
original.licence: CBETA CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 (text quoted for reference)

paraphrase: Seventh doubt: why not seek Maitreya's Tuṣita? They seem alike but differ greatly: even keeping the ten goods one may not be born in Tuṣita, which has no vow-power to receive beings, whereas Amitābha's vow and light embrace all who recollect him; Tuṣita is in the desire realm where many fall back and heavenly women arouse sensual attachment, while in the West all is Mahāyāna and passions never arise.
speaker: (attrib.) Zhiyi

original.text: 但論生彼國，無女人及無盲、聾、瘖、瘂人，不道此間女人、根缺人不得生。
original.edition: Taishō T47n1961 (CBETA XML P5, local copy sources_raw/cbeta), 80b18-19
original.licence: CBETA CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 (text quoted for reference)

paraphrase: Ninth doubt: the West is ten trillion lands away, and the Rebirth Treatise says women and those with deficient faculties are not born there. Answer: distance is spoken of for ordinary eyes — the mind settled at death is already the mind born there, as in a dream one is elsewhere at once; and the verse means that in that land there are no women and no blind or deaf, not that women or the disabled of this world cannot be born — Vaidehī and her five hundred women were promised birth; once born they no longer take such bodies.
speaker: (attrib.) Zhiyi

original.text: 欲決定生西方者，具有二種行，定得生彼：一者、厭離行；二者、欣願行。
original.edition: Taishō T47n1961 (CBETA XML P5, local copy sources_raw/cbeta), 80c01-02
original.licence: CBETA CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 (text quoted for reference)

paraphrase: Tenth doubt: what practice ensures birth, and can householders who have not ended sexual desire be born? Two practices: loathing — contemplating the body as impure (seven kinds of impurity, from seed to death) so as gradually to turn from the five desires even if one cannot yet give up one's wife; and joyful aspiration — aspiring to the Pure Land, contemplating the Buddha and dedicating all merit.
speaker: (attrib.) Zhiyi

original.text: 作斯業者，專念彌陀，一切善根迴生彼國；彌陀本願，誓度娑婆，上盡現生一形、下至臨終十念，俱能決定，皆得往生。
original.edition: Taishō T47n1964 (CBETA XML P5, local copy sources_raw/cbeta), 104a21-23
original.licence: CBETA CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 (text quoted for reference)

paraphrase: Those who do this work single-mindedly recollect Amitābha and dedicate all roots of good to birth there; Amitābha's original vow is to save the Sahā world — from a whole life's practice down to ten recitations at death, all are certainly born; since students doubt because scriptures seem to conflict, fourteen points are harmonised.
speaker: (attrib.) Kuiji

original.text: 然夫眾生心性，融通無礙，泰若虛空，湛猶巨海。若虛空故，其體平等，無別相而可得，何有淨、穢之處？猶巨海故，其性潤滑，能隨緣而不逆，豈無動、靜之時。
original.edition: Taishō T47n1965 (CBETA XML P5, local copy sources_raw/cbeta), 110b16-19
original.licence: CBETA CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 (text quoted for reference)

paraphrase: The mind-nature of beings interpenetrates without obstruction, vast as space and deep as the ocean: being like space, its substance is equal and without distinct marks — where then are pure and impure places? Being like the ocean, it follows conditions — how could it lack moving and still times? So, stirred by the winds of dust it sinks into the five turbidities, or following the Buddha's teaching it returns to the source.
speaker: (attrib.) Wonhyo

original.text: 然念佛三昧是真無上深妙禪門矣。以彌陀法王四十八願名號為佛事，願力度眾生
original.edition: Taishō T47n1983 (CBETA XML P5, local copy sources_raw/cbeta), 474c25-27
original.licence: CBETA CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 (text quoted for reference)

paraphrase: The samādhi of recollecting the Buddha is the truly unsurpassed, profound and wondrous gate of meditation; Amitābha, king of the Dharma, performs the Buddha's work through the name of his forty-eight vows and saves beings by the power of his vow; the voices of the five-tone recitation reach the eternal palace. Those who reject the golden form as mere marks and the teaching as mere words fall into wrong views.
speaker: Fazhao

original.text: 第一會平聲緩念 南無阿彌陀佛。第二會平上聲緩念 南無阿彌陀佛。第三會非緩非急念 南無阿彌陀佛。第四會漸急念 南無阿彌陀佛。第五會四字轉急念 阿彌陀佛。
original.edition: Taishō T47n1983 (CBETA XML P5, local copy sources_raw/cbeta), 476b27-c02
original.licence: CBETA CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 (text quoted for reference)

paraphrase: The five assemblies of recitation: first, 'Namo Amituofo' slowly in level tone; second, slowly in level and rising tones; third, neither slow nor fast; fourth, gradually faster; fifth, the four syllables 'Amituofo' ever faster; then hymns of the jewel birds and others are chanted.
speaker: Fazhao

original.text: 修心之人成道捷徑，法華三昧不輕之行，念佛三昧般舟之宗，僉為無上深妙禪門者，願聞其致。
original.edition: Taishō T47n1967 (CBETA XML P5, local copy sources_raw/cbeta), 134a07-09
original.licence: CBETA CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 (text quoted for reference)

paraphrase: A visitor asks Feixi to explain why the Lotus samādhi of Sadāparibhūta's practice and the nianfo samādhi of the Pratyutpanna are both called the unsurpassed, profound and wondrous gate of meditation and the shortcut to the way; the treatise answers in twenty gates.
speaker: Feixi

original.text: 遠乃於精舍無量壽像前建齋立誓，共期西方。乃令劉遺民著其文曰：惟歲在攝提秋，七月戊辰朔，二十八日乙未。法師釋慧遠貞感幽奧，宿懷特發。乃延命同志息心貞信之士，百有二十三人，集於廬山之陰，般若臺精舍阿彌陀像前，率以香華敬廌而誓焉
original.edition: Taishō T50n2059 (CBETA XML P5, local copy sources_raw/cbeta), 358c21-26
original.licence: CBETA CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 (text quoted for reference)

paraphrase: Lay men of letters such as Liu Yimin, Lei Cizong, Zhou Xuzhi and Zong Bing gathered round Huiyuan; before the image of Amitāyus in the monastery he held a feast and made a vow with them, together aspiring to the West. Liu Yimin wrote the vow: in the year of shetige (402), on the 28th of the seventh month, Huiyuan and 123 like-minded persons gathered before the Amitābha image at the Prajñā terrace on Lushan and, offering incense and flowers, vowed — knowing that retribution follows karma and that the evil paths are hard to escape — to help one another to birth there.
speaker: narrator (Huijiao; vow text by Liu Yimin)
notes: The Gaoseng zhuan does not use the names 'White Lotus Society' or 'eighteen worthies', which appear in later sources (Fozu tongji fasc. 26 lists 蓮社十八賢).

location.section: T1856, the question on the pratyutpanna samādhi

paraphrase: Huiyuan asks Kumārajīva whether the buddha seen in the pratyutpanna samādhi — said by the sūtra to be like things seen in a dream — is produced by one's own mind or is a real buddha coming from outside; if made by the mind, how can it answer questions and resolve doubts? Kumārajīva answers that the sūtra's dream simile shows only that one sees as clearly as in a dream, not that the vision is false; the samādhi is attained by the power of the Buddha, of the samādhi and of one's own merit.
speaker: Huiyuan; Kumārajīva
notes: T45 not in local corpus; content recalled (moderate).

location.section: T2060 fasc. 27, appendix to the section on self-sacrifice (遺身篇)

original.text: 近有山僧善導者。周遊寰寓求訪道津。行至西河遇道綽部。惟行念佛彌陀淨業。既入京師廣行此化。寫彌陀經數萬卷。士女奉者其數無量。時在光明寺說法。有人告導曰。今念佛名定生淨土不。導曰。念佛定生。其人禮拜訖。口誦南無阿彌陀佛聲聲相次出光明寺門。上柳樹表。合掌西望。倒投身下。至地遂死。
original.edition: Taishō T50n2060 (CBETA XML P5, local copy sources_raw/cbeta), 684a11-19
original.licence: CBETA CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 (text quoted for reference)

paraphrase: Recently a mountain monk Shandao, seeking the way everywhere, met Daochuo's community at Xihe and practised only the Pure Land work of recollecting Amitābha; in the capital he spread it widely and copied the Amitābha Sūtra tens of thousands of times. While he was preaching at the Guangming si, a man asked whether reciting the name would surely bring birth in the Pure Land; Shandao said it would. The man bowed, left the temple reciting 'Namo Amituofo' voice after voice, climbed a willow, joined his palms facing west, threw himself down and died.
speaker: narrator (Daoxuan)

differs_from.note: The Song Fozu tongji attributes the leap from the willow to Shandao himself.

notes: The earliest account (Daoxuan, 7th c.) places the episode in the section on self-sacrifice; recorded as a narrative, not as a teaching to be followed.

location.section: T2035 fasc. 26, Treatise on the Establishment of the Pure Land Teaching 12.1

original.text: 蓮社七祖 始祖廬山辯覺正覺圓悟法師 二祖長安光明法師 三祖南岳般舟法師 四祖長安五會法師 五祖新定臺岩法師 六祖永明智覺法師 七祖昭慶圓淨法師
original.edition: Taishō T49n2035 (CBETA XML P5, local copy sources_raw/cbeta), 260c19-24
original.licence: CBETA CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 (text quoted for reference)

paraphrase: The seven patriarchs of the Lotus society: first, the Dharma master of Lushan (Huiyuan); second, the master of Guangming in Chang'an (Shandao); third, the pratyutpanna master of Nanyue (Chengyuan); fourth, the five-tone master of Chang'an (Fazhao); fifth, the master of Taiyan in Xinding (Shaokang); sixth, the Chan master Zhijue of Yongming (Yanshou); seventh, the master Yuanjing of Zhaoqing (Shengchang).
speaker: Zhipan

original.text: 師居山三十年。迹不入俗。唯以淨土克勤於念。初十一年澄心繫想。三覩聖相沈厚不言。後十九年七月晦夕。於般若臺之東龕方從定起。見阿彌陀佛身滿虛空。
original.edition: Taishō T49n2035 (CBETA XML P5, local copy sources_raw/cbeta), 262c16-19
original.licence: CBETA CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 (text quoted for reference)

paraphrase: Huiyuan lived thirty years on the mountain without entering the world, diligent only in recollection for the Pure Land. In the first eleven years, with clear mind and fixed thought, he three times saw the holy form but kept silent. In the nineteenth year (of Yixi, 416), on the last evening of the seventh month, rising from samādhi in the eastern niche of the Prajñā terrace he saw Amitābha filling space, with transformation buddhas in his halo and the two bodhisattvas; streams of light in fourteen branches proclaimed suffering, emptiness, impermanence and no-self; the Buddha said: 'By the power of my original vow I have come to comfort you; in seven days you will be born in my land.' He also saw deceased companions who asked why he was so late.
speaker: Zhipan

original.text: 或問念佛生淨土耶。師曰。如汝所念遂汝所願。乃自念一聲有一光明從其口出。十至於百光亦如之。……唯有徑路修行。但念阿彌陀佛。後忽謂人曰。此身可厭吾將西歸。乃登柳樹向西願曰。願佛接我菩薩助我。令我不失正念得生安養。言已投身自絕。
original.edition: Taishō T49n2035 (CBETA XML P5, local copy sources_raw/cbeta), 263b08-17
original.licence: CBETA CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 (text quoted for reference)

paraphrase: Shandao, having seen Daochuo's nine-grade assembly, said this contemplation gate alone quickly transcends birth-and-death; he recited kneeling until exhausted, sweating even in the cold, did not lie down for over thirty years, kept the precepts minutely, copied the Amitābha Sūtra a hundred thousand times and painted three hundred Pure Land tableaux. Asked whether recollection brings birth, he said 'as you recollect, so your wish is fulfilled', and at each recitation a light came from his mouth. His verse: 'the skin grows wrinkled, the hair white ... only the direct path of practice: just recollect Amitābha.' Later, saying 'this body is loathsome, I shall go west', he climbed a willow, prayed facing west that the Buddha receive him without loss of right mindfulness, and threw himself down; the emperor named his temple Guangming.
speaker: Zhipan

differs_from.note: Daoxuan's earlier account ascribes the leap to a man who questioned Shandao, not to Shandao.

notes: The tradition's accounts differ; recorded as narrative.

original.text: 蓮社之立既以遠公為始祖，自師歸寂，抵今大宋慶元五年己未，凡八百九年矣，中間繼此道者乃有五師：一曰善導師、二曰法照師、三曰少康師、四曰省常師、五曰宗賾師。
original.edition: Taishō T47n1969A (CBETA XML P5, local copy sources_raw/cbeta), 192c19-22
original.licence: CBETA CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 (text quoted for reference)

paraphrase: Since the Lotus society took the master of Lushan (Huiyuan) as its first patriarch, in the 809 years to 1199 five masters have continued the way: Shandao, Fazhao, Shaokang, Shengchang and Zongze.
speaker: Zongxiao

original.text: 問：「唯心淨土，周遍十方。何得託質蓮臺，寄形安養，而興取捨之念，豈達無生之門？欣厭情生，何成平等？」答：「唯心佛土者，了心方生。……又平等之門，無生之旨，雖即仰教生信，其乃力量未充，觀淺心浮，境強習重；須生佛國，以仗勝緣，忍力易成，速行菩薩道。
original.edition: Taishō T48n2017 (CBETA XML P5, local copy sources_raw/cbeta), 966b26-c08
original.licence: CBETA CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 (text quoted for reference)

paraphrase: Objection: the mind-only pure land pervades the ten directions; why lodge in a lotus in Sukhāvatī, giving rise to choosing and rejecting — how is that the gate of non-arising, where is equality? Yanshou: the mind-only buddha-land is born only when the mind is understood; the sūtra says a bodhisattva who knows all is mind-only may be born quickly in Abhirati or Sukhāvatī. Though one believes in equality and non-arising, one's power is not yet sufficient, contemplation is shallow, the mind floats, objects are strong and habits heavy — so one must be born in a buddha-land, relying on its superior conditions, where acceptance is easily achieved and the bodhisattva path swiftly practised (citing the Awakening of Faith).
speaker: Yongming Yanshou
notes: The 'four alternatives' (四料簡) traditionally ascribed to Yanshou were searched for and not found in T2017.

original.text: 十念門者，每日清晨服飾已後，面西正立，合掌連聲稱阿彌陀佛，盡一氣為一念。如是十氣，名為十念。但隨氣長短，不限佛數。……名此為十念者，顯是藉氣束心也。
original.edition: Taishō T47n1968 (CBETA XML P5, local copy sources_raw/cbeta), 147a17-22
original.licence: CBETA CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 (text quoted for reference)

paraphrase: The gate of ten recitations: each morning after dressing, stand facing west, join the palms and call Amitābha's name continuously for the length of one breath — that is one 'recitation'; ten breaths are the ten recitations; the number of names follows the breath's length, not a count; the voice neither high nor low, neither slow nor hurried. It is called ten recitations because the breath is used to bind the mind. Then one makes the vow of dedication, recalling the eighteenth vow, asking that at death one know the time, be free of pain and craving, and be welcomed by the Buddha and holy ones.
speaker: Ciyun Zunshi
notes: Natural breathing while reciting; not a retention practice.

original.text: 我心既然，生佛體等，如此則方了迴神億剎，實生乎自己心中；孕質九蓮，豈逃乎剎那際內。
original.edition: Taishō T47n1968 (CBETA XML P5, local copy sources_raw/cbeta), 145c11-13
original.licence: CBETA CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 (text quoted for reference)

paraphrase: Because mind, buddha and beings are one in substance, turning one's spirit to a land ten trillion lands away is really to be born within one's own mind, and being conceived in the nine-grade lotus does not escape the present instant; unless phenomena and principle interpenetrate, how could a five-offence ordinary being reach the jewelled land by ten recitations?
speaker: Ciyun Zunshi

original.text: 勸人歸依三寶、受持五戒，一不殺、二不盜、三不婬、四不妄、五不酒，念阿彌陀佛五聲以證五戒，普結淨緣，欲令世人淨五根、得五力、出五濁也。
original.edition: Taishō T47n1973 (CBETA XML P5, local copy sources_raw/cbeta), 326a19-22
original.licence: CBETA CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 (text quoted for reference)

paraphrase: Mao Ziyuan, after awakening in samādhi at a crow's cry, emulated Huiyuan's Lotus society: he urged people to take refuge and keep the five precepts, reciting Amitābha's name five times to confirm the five precepts, so that they might purify the five roots, gain the five powers and leave the five turbidities; he compiled a dawn repentance liturgy of the Lotus school and founded a repentance hall at Dianshan lake.
speaker: Pudu (narrator)

original.text: 此則知諸剎諸塵塵塵皆唯心之極樂也，一塵一佛佛佛皆本性之彌陀也。……心垢土垢、心淨土淨。……夫欲淨其心有，捨淨土之修法，他無能焉。
original.edition: Taishō T47n1972 (CBETA XML P5, local copy sources_raw/cbeta), 295a13-23
original.licence: CBETA CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 (text quoted for reference)

paraphrase: Thus every land and every mote is the Land of Bliss of mind-only, every buddha in every mote is the Amitābha of one's own nature. Why then is the Sahā world impure? Ordinary beings' karma makes the pure impure, while the Buddha's eye sees the impure as pure. If the mind is defiled the land is defiled, if pure the land is pure — and to purify the mind there is no method apart from Pure Land practice, which has three gates: contemplation, recollection and the many practices, all taking Amitābha of the Land of Bliss as lord.
speaker: Tianru Weize

original.text: 一真法性中，具足十法界，依正本融通，生佛非殊致。
original.edition: Taishō T47n1975 (CBETA XML P5, local copy sources_raw/cbeta), 381b07-08
original.licence: CBETA CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 (text quoted for reference)

paraphrase: Chuandeng sets out ten gates (one true dharma-realm; the arising of body and land; mind and land identical; beings and buddhas not two; ...). The first verse: within the one true dharma-nature the ten dharma-realms are complete; the environment and the person are fundamentally interfused; beings and buddhas do not differ. The one true dharma-realm is beings' inherent mind-nature, endowed with countless virtues.
speaker: Youxi Chuandeng

original.text: 歸元性無二，方便有多門。曉得此意，禪宗、淨土，殊途同歸。……如中峰大師道：『禪者，淨土之禪；淨土者，禪之淨土。而修之者必貴一門深入。』
original.edition: Taishō T47n1977 (CBETA XML P5, local copy sources_raw/cbeta), 420a13-17
original.licence: CBETA CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 (text quoted for reference)

paraphrase: Asked whether Pure Land is only a symbol and the wise should awaken directly through Chan: 'returning to the source the nature is not two; expedient means have many gates' — Chan and Pure Land reach the same end by different roads.
